rounds.text: The market is profoundly mispricing EIH Associated Hotels Ltd by anchoring to short-term noise while ignoring a powerful structural acceleration in top-line expansion, evidenced by a 31% compounded sales growth rate over five years [E15]. This is compounded by superior capital efficiency, with return on assets at 3.57% outperforming the sector benchmark of 3.5% [E8]. Furthermore, the company is actively laying the foundation for future capacity and earnings expansion, as demonstrated by a massive 176.5% surge in capital work-in-progress to ₹47 crore by March 2026 [E41]. Trading at a modest trailing P/E of 21.6 based on filed statements [E1], the equity sits deeply depressed at just 31% of its 52-week range [E5], offering an extraordinary entry point given that profit growth currently exceeds one-year price growth by 14% [E57]. Conceded: [E16], [E17], [E67], [E68].

Conceded: [E15]. The bull's reliance on a 31% five-year compounded sales growth rate [E15] is severely undermined by severe recent deceleration, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of just 4% [E16] and a negative trailing twelve-month growth rate of -6% [E17], alongside a -9% year-over-year sales screen reason [E67] and decelerating earnings growth [E68]. Furthermore, the claim of a depressed valuation at 31% of the 52-week range [E5] ignores the fact that the price-to-book ratio of 2.95x is more than triple the sector benchmark of 0.95x [E7], indicating a rich valuation rather than a bargain. Conceded: [E8]. While return on assets slightly beats the sector benchmark [E8], this does not justify the massive 176.5% build-up in capital work-in-progress to ₹47 Cr by March 2026 [E41], which represents unyielding execution risk during a period of contracting top-line performance.
